stories.headline: DeepSeek Releases V4-Pro (1.6T Params) and V4-Flash, Largest Open-Source Models With 1M Context

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek-V4-Pro has 1.6T total parameters with 49B active (MoE), pre-trained on 33T tokens. V4-Flash has 284B total with 13B active, trained on 32T tokens. Both support 1M token context.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek-V4-Pro: 1.6T total / 49B active params. Performance rivaling the world's top closed-source models. DeepSeek-V4-Flash: 284B total / 13B active params. Your fast, efficient, and economical choice.

key_facts.fact: V4-Pro is the largest open-weights model released, bigger than Kimi K2.6 (1.1T) and GLM-5.1 (754B), and more than twice the size of DeepSeek V3.2 (685B).
key_facts.excerpt: I think this makes DeepSeek-V4-Pro the new largest open weights model. It's larger than Kimi K2.6 (1.1T) and GLM-5.1 (754B) and more than twice the size of DeepSeek V3.2 (685B).

key_facts.fact: V4-Pro API pricing is $1.74/1M input tokens and $3.48/1M output; V4-Flash is $0.14/1M input and $0.28/1M output — the cheapest in both model tiers.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek-V4-Flash is the cheapest of the small models, beating even OpenAI's GPT-5.4 Nano. DeepSeek-V4-Pro is the cheapest of the larger frontier models.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek says V4-Pro trails state-of-the-art frontier models (GPT-5.4 and Gemini 3.1-Pro) by approximately 3 to 6 months, and is the strongest open-source model in coding and math benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: Against the current closed-source frontier, OpenAI's GPT-5.4 and Gemini 3.1-Pro — the company says V4-Pro falls only 'marginally short,' and offers a candid self-assessment: its 'developmental trajectory' trails state-of-the-art frontier models by approximately 3 to 6 months.

key_facts.fact: V4 introduces a hybrid attention mechanism (Compressed Sparse Attention + Heavily Compressed Attention) that reduces KV cache to 10% and single-token FLOPs to 27% of V3.2 at 1M context.
key_facts.excerpt: In the scenario of 1M-token context, even DeepSeek-V4-Pro attains only 27% of the single-token FLOPs and 10% of the KV cache size relative to DeepSeek-V3.2.

key_facts.fact: Both models are open-sourced under the MIT license on Hugging Face. The release was timed to coincide with OpenAI's GPT-5.5 launch on the same day.
key_facts.excerpt: This repository and the model weights are licensed under the MIT License.

key_facts.fact: Huawei announced its Ascend supernode based on the Ascend 950 AI chips will fully support DeepSeek V4. DeepSeek says V4-Pro throughput is currently limited by high-end compute supply, with prices expected to drop when Huawei Ascend 950 super nodes ship at scale in H2.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek worked with Chinese AI chipmakers Huawei and Cambricon to optimise V4 for their latest hardware. The company did not give Nvidia or AMD early access for optimisation.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.5 With Gains in Agentic Coding and Computer Use, Priced at $5/$30 Per 1M Tokens

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.5 released April 23, six weeks after GPT-5.4. It scores 82.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, beating Claude Opus 4.7 (69.4%) and Gemini 3.1 Pro (68.5%). On OSWorld-Verified it scores 78.7% vs Claude Opus 4.7 at 78.0%.
key_facts.excerpt: Terminal-Bench 2.0: GPT-5.5 82.7%, GPT-5.4 75.1%, Claude Opus 4.7 69.4%, Gemini 3.1 Pro 68.5%. OSWorld-Verified: GPT-5.5 78.7%, Claude Opus 4.7 78.0%, GPT-5.4 75.0%.

key_facts.fact: On SWE-Bench Pro (real GitHub issue resolution), GPT-5.5 scores 58.6%, while Claude Opus 4.7 scores 64.3% — Anthropic still leads in production coding.
key_facts.excerpt: On SWE-Bench Pro, which grades real-world GitHub issue resolution, it reaches 58.6%. Claude Opus 4.7 scores higher at 64.3%.

key_facts.fact: API pricing is $5/1M input tokens and $30/1M output tokens — double GPT-5.4. GPT-5.5 Pro costs $30/1M input and $180/1M output. Both have a 1M token context window.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-5.5: $5.00 input, $0.50 cached input, $30.00 output per million tokens. GPT-5.5 Pro: $30.00 input, $3.00 cached input, $180.00 output.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI claims GPT-5.5 uses ~40% fewer output tokens for equivalent tasks, bringing the effective net cost increase to around 20% despite the doubled per-token price.
key_facts.excerpt: It uses about 40% fewer output tokens for equivalent tasks, which keeps the real net cost increase closer to 20%. The five distinct effort levels also give you flexible cost control.

key_facts.fact: Rolling out to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in ChatGPT and Codex. GPT-5.5 was co-designed and trained on Nvidia's GB200 and GB300 NVL72 systems.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-5.5 is now available to paying users of ChatGPT and the coding tool Codex across the Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise tiers. GPT-5.5 was co-designed and trained on Nvidia's next-generation AI chips, the GB200 and GB300 NVL72 systems.

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.5 matches GPT-5.4 per-token latency in real-world serving despite higher capability. OpenAI leads the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 60, three points ahead of Claude Opus 4.7 and Gemini 3.1 Pro at 57.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-5.5 is OpenAI's new flagship model, released April 23, 2026. It leads the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 60, putting it three points ahead of Claude Opus 4.7 and Gemini 3.1 Pro at 57.

stories.headline: Cohere Acquires Germany's Aleph Alpha in $20B Sovereign AI Deal, Schwarz Group Invests $600M

key_facts.fact: Canadian AI startup Cohere agreed to acquire German AI startup Aleph Alpha in a deal valuing the combined entity at approximately $20 billion. Cohere shareholders receive ~90% of the combined company, Aleph Alpha's ~10%.
key_facts.excerpt: Cohere's shareholders will receive approximately 90% of the combined entity, while Aleph's shareholders are expected to receive approximately 10%. The combined valuation of $20 billion reflects a significant premium over both companies' last known marks.

key_facts.fact: Schwarz Group, which owns retailers Lidl and Kaufland, will invest $600 million in Cohere's upcoming Series E round as part of the deal. Cohere was last valued at $6.8 billion in August 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Schwarz Group — a key backer of Aleph Alpha — plans to invest $600 million in Cohere's upcoming Series E round. Cohere last raised $500 million in fresh capital in August 2025, bringing its valuation to $6.8 billion.

key_facts.fact: Global HQ stays in Toronto, European HQ in Berlin. Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez remains CEO. Germany's Digital Minister Karsten Wildberger and Canada's AI Minister Evan Solomon attended the Berlin announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: The combined entity will have its global headquarters in Toronto and its European headquarters in Berlin. The deal is supported by the Canadian and German governments.

key_facts.fact: The deal targets sovereign AI for regulated sectors — public sector, finance, defense, energy, healthcare — giving Cohere access to Aleph Alpha's existing German government contracts including the ministry for digital affairs.
key_facts.excerpt: Cohere will look to boost its offering of secure customized AI for highly-regulated sectors. Aleph Alpha's existing commercial contracts with the German public sector were also an attraction.

key_facts.fact: Cohere CFO Francois Chadwick told Reuters: 'We are going to commit to working with European infrastructure and maintain the sovereignty requirements that are being addressed in Europe.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'We are bringing Aleph Alpha into Cohere, and we are going to merge the two entities,' Cohere CFO Francois Chadwick told Reuters. 'We are going to commit to working with European infrastructure … and maintain the sovereignty requirements.'

stories.headline: Anthropic Hits $1 Trillion Valuation on Secondary Markets, Surpassing OpenAI's $880B on Forge Global

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's valuation on Forge Global, a leading private marketplace exchange, has hit approximately $1 trillion, surpassing OpenAI which trades at $880 billion on the same platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Desperate buyers are in a race to secure a dwindling supply of secondary shares in Anthropic. One shareholder recently offered to sell shares at a $1.15 trillion valuation.

key_facts.fact: On Hiive, another secondary marketplace, Anthropic share prices surged 211% to roughly $900 over the past three months, while OpenAI shares rose only 8.5% to $608 in the same period.
key_facts.excerpt: Private stock market Hiive informed The Post that the price for Anthropic shares has surged 211% to roughly $900 over the previous three months. Shares of OpenAI have risen just 8.5% to $608 over the same period.

key_facts.fact: The surge is driven by Anthropic's rapid revenue growth — from $9 billion at end of 2025 to over $30 billion by end of March 2026 — and strong adoption of Claude Code.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has also seen enormous income growth, from $9 billion at the finish of 2025 to over $30 billion by the finish of March. The company credited widespread adoption of its commercially accessible Claude services for the surge.

key_facts.fact: Glen Anderson, CEO of Rainmaker Securities, said he received an offer to buy Anthropic shares at a $960 billion valuation — 'an unthinkable price even just weeks ago.' A separate offer from a 'very well-known growth fund' came in at $1.05 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: 'It's been an epic run for Anthropic,' Glen Anderson, CEO of Rainmaker Securities, said. 'Everybody desires to be half of a generational alternative in AI, and proper now, Anthropic is in the pole place.'

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's last primary funding round valued the company at $380 billion; the secondary market premium implies ~2.6x that valuation. OpenAI's last primary round was $852 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has a $1 trillion secondary market valuation compared to a $380 billion actual valuation, possibly signaling more room for growth. Meanwhile, OpenAI's secondary valuation of $880 billion is just $30 billion less than the actual $850 billion valuation.

stories.headline: Anthropic Publishes Postmortem on Claude Code Quality Drop: Three Bugs Fixed, Usage Limits Reset

key_facts.fact: Anthropic traced Claude Code quality complaints to three separate changes: reduced default reasoning effort (March 4), a caching bug that cleared thinking every turn (March 26), and a system prompt limiting responses to ≤25 words between tool calls (April 16).
key_facts.excerpt: We've traced these reports to three separate changes that affected Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK, and Claude Cowork. The API was not impacted.

key_facts.fact: The reasoning effort change reduced default from 'high' to 'medium' to cut latency; Anthropic called it 'the wrong tradeoff' and reverted on April 7. All users now default to 'xhigh' for Opus 4.7 and 'high' for other models.
key_facts.excerpt: We changed Claude Code's default reasoning effort from 'high' to 'medium' to reduce the very long latency. This was the wrong tradeoff. We reverted this change on April 7.

key_facts.fact: The caching bug was meant to clear old thinking from idle sessions once, but instead cleared it every turn, making Claude 'forgetful and repetitive.' It passed multiple layers of review before being caught.
key_facts.excerpt: A bug caused this to keep happening every turn for the rest of the session instead of just once, which made Claude seem forgetful and repetitive.

key_facts.fact: The verbosity-reduction system prompt caused a measurable 3% drop in coding benchmarks for both Opus 4.6 and 4.7, and was reverted on April 20. All issues resolved in v2.1.116.
key_facts.excerpt: One of these evaluations showed a 3% drop for both Opus 4.6 and 4.7. We immediately reverted the prompt as part of the April 20 release.

key_facts.fact: As compensation, Anthropic reset usage limits for all subscribers. The company also set up the @ClaudeDevs X account for more transparent communication of product decisions.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropics also set up the X account @ClaudeDevs to communicate product decisions more transparently.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is adding tighter controls: broader per-model eval suites for every system prompt change, soak periods, gradual rollouts, and new tooling to make prompt changes easier to review and audit.
key_facts.excerpt: We're also adding tighter controls on system prompt changes. We will run a broad suite of per-model evals for every system prompt change to Claude Code.

stories.headline: AI Coding Startup Cognition in Early Funding Talks at $25B Valuation, Up From $10.2B in September

key_facts.fact: Cognition AI is in early talks to raise hundreds of millions of dollars or more at a $25 billion valuation, more than doubling its $10.2 billion valuation from September 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Cognition AI Inc. is reportedly in discussions with investors for a significant funding round that would more than double its valuation to $25 billion.

key_facts.fact: Cognition is best known for Devin, which the company bills as an autonomous AI software engineer that automates code creation, debugging, and deployment. Customers include Dell and Cisco.
key_facts.excerpt: Cognition is known for its AI software engineer, Devin, which automates complex engineering tasks. The firm's customers include Dell Technologies Inc., Cisco Systems Inc. and numerous tech giants.

key_facts.fact: The company acquired Windsurf in July 2025 and annual recurring revenue has more than doubled since that acquisition. Devin's ARR grew from $1M in September 2024 to $73M by June 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: In July 2025, it bought Windsurf, its product Devin grew annual recurring revenue from $1 million in September 2024 to $73 million by June 2025. Since buying Windsurf, Cognition's annual recurring revenue has more than doubled.

key_facts.fact: The funding talks were already underway when SpaceX announced its $60 billion deal for Cursor, adding fuel to AI coding valuations.
key_facts.excerpt: Cognition is trying to tap into the growing momentum around AI-generated code that's primarily driven by competitors such as Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC.

stories.headline: Cursor Hit $2.7B Annualized Revenue in March, Up 14x YoY, as Gross Margins Turn Positive

key_facts.fact: Cursor hit $2.7 billion in annualized revenue in March 2026, 14 times higher than a year ago. Investors expect annualized revenue to exceed $7 billion by year-end.
key_facts.excerpt: AI coding startup Cursor last month hit $2.7 billion in annualized revenue, 14 times higher than that revenue pace a year ago. Some investors expected annualized revenue to hit more than $7 billion by year's end.

key_facts.fact: Cursor's gross margins have turned positive after being at -23% in January 2026, helped by cost structure optimizations and the launch of the Composer model.
key_facts.excerpt: Following the launch of the Composer model in November 2025 and cost structure optimizations, the company recently turned gross margin positive, with its enterprise business—which accounts for approximately 60% of revenue—already achieving positive gross margins.

key_facts.fact: Cursor recently agreed to a potential $60 billion acquisition by SpaceX, or a $10 billion collaboration fee. SpaceX isn't acquiring immediately due to its imminent IPO targeting a $2 trillion valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX said it has an agreement giving it the right to acquire artificial intelligence startup Cursor for $60 billion later this year or to pay $10 billion for the companies' work together.

key_facts.fact: Cursor had been days from closing a separate $2 billion funding round at a $50 billion valuation when the SpaceX deal halted those talks. Microsoft had also looked at a Cursor acquisition before SpaceX moved and chose not to proceed.
key_facts.excerpt: Cursor was days from closing a separate $2 billion funding round at a $50 billion valuation — investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Nvidia, and Thrive Capital were caught off guard. Microsoft had also looked at a potential acquisition of Cursor before SpaceX moved, and chose not.

key_facts.fact: Cursor pays retail prices to Anthropic and OpenAI — the same companies competing against it with Claude Code and Codex. SpaceX's compute infrastructure would restructure those unit economics.
key_facts.excerpt: Cursor currently pays retail prices to Anthropic and OpenAI to the same companies competing directly against it with Claude Code and Codex. That means every dollar of revenue Cursor earns partially funds its own competition.
